verdict.line: Buy only below $2,700 psf. A 3-bed here at about $2,630 psf is a little above what the closest competitors' 3-bed-size resales support (about $2,570 psf as a new launch), so negotiate or choose a cheaper stack. 3-bed and 4-bed are the most wanted sizes in this mixed own-stay and rental area.
reasons: The closest competitors (Clavon, The Clement Canopy, Seahill, The Vision, Hundred Trees) work out to about $2,570 psf as a brand-new launch, after adding 5% where they were not built under the harmonised floor-area rules, a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (13% to 41% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 8% over a just-completed resale and about 2.6 points more for each year of its age (29 launches against 102 of their resale competitors, this one and the 6 most extreme pairs left out).

Clavon (121 m away, 640 homes, completed 2024): its 3-bed-size resales (about 790 to 1,060 sq ft) averaged $2,249 psf over the last 12 months (5 resales), against a median $2,159 psf for all sizes. A 3-bed here at about $2,628 psf is $379 psf (+17%) above that; a 3-bed there sold for a median $2.68M.

The newest land bid nearby, Dover Drive (GLS) (1,823 m, $1,556 psf ppr), is 24% above this site's land cost. It breaks even at about $2,570 psf, and analysts expect it to launch at $2,800-2,900+ (CBRE, PropNex).

compsNote: 2 of the 5 competitors are within 1 km. Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3; executive condos are left out. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Where a competitor has too few resales of a size, that size is estimated from its own nearest size, so every unit type is judged against the same competitors. Each is raised by a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (13% to 41% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 8% over a just-completed resale and about 2.6 points more for each year of its age (29 launches against 102 of their resale competitors, this one and the 6 most extreme pairs left out). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size (a launch nearby from the last 2 years counts for half); walk away above = 5% more. 3-bed: buy at or below $2,570, walk away above $2,700, this project about $2,628 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $2,600, walk away above $2,730, this project about $2,505 psf. This project's price by unit type is from the developer's caveats. The developer breaks even at about $2,160 psf (EdgeProp's method); launches since 2023 priced on average 27% above break-even, which points to about $2,750 psf.

fplans.note: Main layout per bedroom type (most units where counts are published), redrawn from the developers' plans in the Stacked Homes directory. Score out of 10, same rules for every plan: start at 4; +1 regular shape, dumbbell, kitchen that can be closed off, kitchen or yard window, AC ledge and planter under 5%, store or shelter or utility room; −1 long corridor, ledge and planter 10% or more, balcony over 12%. Efficiency = the share of the area not taken by AC ledges, planters, bay windows and corridors. Plans under the 2023 rules exclude AC ledges from the strata area, so their sq ft is all usable.

supply.ring: middle ring (6 to 11 km from the CBD)
concerns: Will too many new condos nearby hurt my price?

Besides this project's own 501 homes, about 1,177 new homes within 2 km launch within about 2 years of it (Nava Grove, Dover Drive (GLS)); the condo resale market within 2 km handles about 575 resales a year. Our test of 19 condos completed 2016 to 2022 in the middle ring (6 to 11 km from the CBD): those with more than 862 other new homes completing within 2 km and 2 years grew 1.9% a year over the past 4 years, against 3.6% for those with fewer (URA caveats). Expect some competition when units complete together, mainly on rents and resale speed, but no collapse: the local buyer pool is deep.
The developer paid more for the land. Am I paying more?

Across 16 launches since 2023, launch prices rose roughly dollar for dollar with break-even (about $103 per $100), so developers kept a similar dollar margin while their percentage margin shrank (22% above break-even on land of $1,200 psf ppr or more, 31% on cheaper land). Part of that is location: dearer land is usually where homes sell for more anyway. So a high bid does show up in prices, but only as far as buyers will pay against nearby homes. The test that protects you is the price against same-size competitors: our buy-at and walk-away prices.
Will the developer cut prices later?
87% sold so far. Developers must sell every unit within 5 years of buying the land or repay most of a 40% stamp duty (IRAS); with most units sold, there is little pressure to cut prices.
Should I wait for the next launch nearby?

The next launch nearby, Dover Drive (GLS), is likely at about $2,800 to $2,900 psf, above this project's 3-bed. Waiting for it is unlikely to get you a cheaper new home here, and a dearer neighbour helps support this project's resale price.

Islandwide, about 18,296 private homes complete in 2027 and 2028 and 15,810 homes in the pipeline were still unsold at mid-2026 (URA). That is enough to keep price growth moderate, but local supply and the local buyer pool matter more for your resale.
